metaphor: A neighbourhood çarşı street at opening time, drawn flat and modern in CSS with no photos. Each category is a dükkân: a hand-painted esnaf tabelası, a striped scalloped tente (awning) under it and a galvanised kepenk (rolling shutter). The shutter's height is real data: firms open now (isOpenNow() true) have their kepenk rolled up, closed firms have it pulled two-thirds down, and firms with no opening hours sit half-way with no label. Locations hang on blue-and-white enamel address plates. The search box is a signboard hanging from two chains. Job posts are 'ELEMAN ARANIYOR' papers in a shop window, and blog posts are gold-leaf (yaldız) lettering on smoked shop glass. The registration CTA is the sector's own idiom: 'Tabelanı as' (hang your sign). The site's whole vocabulary is the shopkeeper's: dükkân, tabela, kepenk, vitrin, eşik, kaldırım, sokak, esnaf.
why_unique: Not a photo hero, not a phone shell, not a map, not a 50/50 split and not a copy-left / 2×3-tiles-right hero. The hero is a stacked composition: a centred hanging-sign search above a full-bleed illustrated street skyline of shopfronts. Against craft-market, the closest relative: craft-market uses brick red, Georgia, a split hero with an asymmetric tile grid and logo 'plinth' cards. Tabela Çarşısı has no split, puts categories in a horizontal street of facades with shutters, and uses slab plus rounded-humanist type in plum, mustard and turquoise. Against solarpunk-market: that theme is a stock street photo under a green veil, while this one is a fully CSS-drawn, data-driven street. Against sun-listing: mustard here only shades sign letters and stripes awnings, with no marker highlight and no yellow page. Against board-v2 and classifieds-board: signs are bolted level onto a wall, with no pins, tape, newsprint or masthead. Against departure-board, metro and signal-station: the enamel plates are addresses, not routes or gates, so there is no transit vocabulary. Against brutalist-directory and acid-poster: depth comes from stacked text-shadow on lettering and soft cast shadows on the wall, never hard offset box shadows. Against paper-trail, design-catalog and cinematic-atlas: no serif masthead and no dateline. The palette is a plum primary (#5c2346) with mustard (#d9a12b) and turquoise (#17877f), a family no existing theme uses (the crowded violets are bright #7c3aed/#8b5cf6). The fonts are Zilla Slab, Alfa Slab One and Nunito, which appear nowhere in the repo. It also drops the overused micro-patterns: no tracked uppercase eyebrows (an enamel plate tag replaces them), no 01/02 numbering, no initial-letter avatar squares and no pill chips. Its one functional idea, kepenk height mapped to isOpenNow(), exists in no other theme.
fonts: Sign lettering (short words only: brand, shopfront signs, category signs, AÇIK/KAPALI stencils, 'ELEMAN ARANIYOR'): Alfa Slab One 400. Headings (H1, H2, firm names on the card signs): Zilla Slab 500/600/700. Body and UI: Nunito 400/600/700/800 (rounded humanist). All three ship the latin-ext subset with full Turkish glyphs (ç ğ ı İ ö ş ü and â î û). ThemeHelper::googleFontsUrl drops weights, so partials/tabela-carsi/styles.blade.php loads its own link, the same way the catalog and board partials do: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Alfa+Slab+One&family=Nunito:wght@400;600;700;800&family=Zilla+Slab:wght@500;600;700&display=swap. Config values: font_heading "'Zilla Slab',Georgia,serif" and font_body "Nunito,sans-serif". Casing rule: never Str::upper (mb_strtoupper turns i into I, not İ). Where uppercase is wanted, use CSS text-transform, which is correct because layouts.app sets html lang="tr". Category and firm names otherwise stay in their natural case, as painted signs usually are.

It is one long painted signboard (plum #5c2346, 72px tall on desktop, 60px on mobile) with a bolt dot in each corner. The bolts are four radial-gradient background layers, so no extra markup. Left: the brand in Alfa Slab One, cream #f8ecd0 lettering with a stacked mustard shade (1px/2px/3px #d9a12b offsets plus a faint 4px rgba(0,0,0,.25)), from settings->site_name or directory->name, linking home. If a logo exists it sits in a small cream enamel roundel before the name. Centre (≥1024px only): Nunito 700 links in cream at 85% opacity, underlined in mustard on hover/focus: Firmalar (companies.index), Meslekler (#tc-sokaklar), Şehirler (#tc-mahalleler), Blog (blog.index). Right: a ghost 'Esnafa sor' link to #tc-ara, then the CTA 'Tabelanı as': mustard fill, ink #1d1a17 text, 6px radius, linking to owner.register. A tente strip, the signature awning, hangs under the board: 16px tall (10px on mobile), vertical plum/cream stripes 14px wide, bottom edge cut into scallops by a mask of radial-gradient half-circles every 16px. Inner pages keep this header, which satisfies the 'header class on inner pages' test.

signature_details: Scalloped striped tente (awning): a repeating-linear-gradient of 90deg stripes, its bottom edge cut by a mask of radial-gradient half-circles every 16px. One component reused under the header, under every shopfront and card sign, and under inner-page heroes via '.theme-tabela-carsi main section[style*=--primary]::after'.

Data-driven kepenk (rolling shutter): repeating 180deg zinc ribs (#b7bcbe / #959b9e / #868d90 shadow) whose covered height encodes isOpenNow() (12% / 62% / 30%) and rises on hover/focus. Open or closed reads at a glance with no legend.

Painted shaded sign lettering: Alfa Slab One in cream with stacked text-shadow offsets in mustard #d9a12b plus a faint dark 4px drop, the 'gölgeli harf' of a signwriter. Used only for short sign words, and depth always comes from text-shadow, never hard box shadows.
Bolt dots in sign corners from four radial-gradient background layers positioned at the corners, so no extra markup is needed.
Navy enamel plates (#1f3566, 2px white rim plus an outer navy ring, screw dots) carry every address: the city grid, the place on each card, the 'Hoş geldiniz' tag and door numbers.

A consistent category tone: crc32(slug) % 6 maps each category to one of mürdüm #5c2346, firuze #17877f, hardal #d9a12b, kiremit #b4532a, zeytin #5d6a2b or plaka #1f3566. The same category keeps its colour across its facade, its wall sign and every card sign.
Hanging signboard search on two CSS chains (dashed 2px pseudo-elements) with a single sway on load (transform-origin top centre), reused as the final blank 'Tabelanı as' sign.

Street skyline: pastel limewash walls (pembe, fıstık, aşı sarısı, açık mavi, kum, lila), nth-child(3n+1) upper storeys with a cornice for a varied roofline, a warm amber interior glow behind each doorway, and a paved sidewalk band with joints every 64px and a stone kerb holding the stat plates.
A very low-contrast brick-bond wall behind the category signs (two linear-gradient layers, mortar #e7e0d4 on #efe8dc). Signs hang level, never rotated or pinned.
Shop-glass treatments: 'ELEMAN ARANIYOR' paper notes behind smoked glass for jobs, and gold-leaf (yaldız) lettering #e2b75a on smoked glass #1f2422 for blog titles.
Empty-slot conversion built into the metaphor: the street's last shopfront is always 'Tabelanı bekliyor' and leftover grid slots become 'Yer boş' cards, all linking to owner.register.

Overused micro-patterns removed on purpose: no tracked uppercase eyebrows, no 01/02 numbering, no pill chips and no initial-letter avatars. Every grid uses repeat(n,minmax(0,1fr)), and single columns use minmax(0,1fr), to satisfy MobileGridStylesTest.

conversion: Searches: the hanging signboard is the first interactive object, a GET to route('search') with q plus a city select (diger-iller excluded). The 'Bugün çok sorulan' links and the 6 shopfronts send people straight into category pages, which also builds strong internal links for SEO. The mobile sticky 'Esnafa sor' keeps search one tap away. Calls: every card's eşik row leads with a plum 'Ara' tel: button and a WhatsApp button. The 'Kepenkler açık' rail serves urgent intent with an 'Ara' on every tile. The kepenk state makes 'open right now' obvious, which raises the chance of a call. Firm registrations: the idiom 'Tabelanı as' runs through the whole page: a header CTA on every page, the always-present blank 'Tabelanı bekliyor' shopfront at the end of the street, 'Yer boş' cards that fill gaps in the grid, the 'Çarşı yeni kuruluyor' empty state, the final hanging blank sign and the mobile sticky bar, all to route('owner.register'). The copy promises 'Ücretsiz başvur, ekibimiz WhatsApp'tan dönsün', so there are no prices and no on-site payment. The page never mentions other directories, a network, 'rehberlerimiz' or 'en büyük'. Counters render only when they are real and large enough (esnaf >= 25, meslek >= 3, şehir >= 3).

metaphor: The whole home page is a glazed İznik tile wall (çini pano), like the panels in an old çeşme, han or hamam. Every category is a square karo. The corners and edge midpoints of each tile carry quarter-rosettes and half-discs, so when the tiles sit side by side across thin grout (derz) lines the motifs join into whole rosettes, the same way real İznik panels split one large pattern over many tiles. The hero is a big white şemse medallion set into a cobalt tile wall, with concentric glaze bands and salbek pendants, and the search sits inside it. Headings sit inside pointed-end kartuş plaques, the way inscriptions are set into tile walls. Stats and cities read as a kitabe, a white inscription on a cobalt band. Firms are glazed plaques. The final call to action is a wall with one tile missing: 'Panoda sizin karonuz eksik'. Coral red (the raised İznik bole red) is used sparingly, as on real tiles: pips, the premium seal and the single register button.
why_unique: No existing theme uses a tessellated tile wall, Turkish ornament, or the cobalt + turquoise + coral glaze triad. Contrasts with the closest themes: (1) verified-trust, premium-showcase and orbit-directory have decorative concentric rings on a gradient or glow. Here the rings are glaze bands (box-shadow) around a solid elliptical medallion inset in a patterned tile wall with grout lines, and they have pendants. (2) mosaic, craft-market, brutalist-directory and category-atlas use bordered or bento category grids where every tile stands alone and some vary in size. Here the tiles are uniform and gapless apart from 3px grout, and the pattern only completes across tile boundaries. Filler tiles are added so the rosettes never break. (3) design-catalog, elegant, cinematic-atlas, paper-trail and city-journal are cream/parchment + rust + Georgia/Fraunces/Playfair editorial. This theme has a cool glaze-white ground (#f3f4ef, not parchment), Alegreya (a calligraphic humanist serif, unused) and Nunito (a rounded humanist, unused), and no masthead or dateline. (4) The blue primaries (default, corporate, ilan-board, signal-station, metro) are flat SaaS/navy. Cobalt here is a glaze colour always paired with turquoise and coral on a patterned ground, never a flat gradient. (5) It is not a photo hero, phone shell, map, 3-column portal, board, transit, ledger, radar or nature theme. It also drops the shared micro-patterns: no uppercase tracked eyebrows, no 01/02 numbering, no stat cards, no pill chips, no initial-letter avatar squares and no 'Firmanı ekle' tile. In their place are cartouches, lozenge separators, a kitabe line, square glazed chips, slug-seeded mini tile placeholders and the missing-tile CTA.
fonts: Headings: Alegreya (Google Fonts, latin-ext subset, full Turkish ğ Ğ ı İ ş Ş ç Ç ö Ö ü Ü). Use 800 for the H1, 700 for H2/H3 and italic 500/600 for the directory-name line, category cartouches and the kitabe inscriptions. Its pen-stroke humanist forms echo the calligraphic cartouches on tile walls. Body: Nunito (latin-ext, full Turkish), 400/600/700/800 at a 16px base and line-height 1.6. Its rounded terminals echo soft glaze edges and it stays very legible on phones. Neither font is used anywhere in the repo. Config: font_heading 'Alegreya,serif', font_body 'Nunito,sans-serif'. ThemeHelper::googleFontsUrl only loads weight 400, so partials/cini-pano/styles.blade.php adds its own preconnect plus a weighted link, as board/catalog do: family=Alegreya:ital,wght@0,500;0,700;0,800;1,500;1,600&family=Nunito:wght@400;600;700;800&display=swap. Numbers use Turkish formatting: number_format(n, 0, ',', '.') and a decimal comma for ratings (4,6).

Hover and focus show a 6px coral lozenge (rotated square) under the link instead of an underline. The layout is not added to PHONE_SHELL or directory_themes.
hero: 'Şemse madalyon in a tile wall'. A full-bleed section `cn-hero` (padding 72px 0 64px) on a cobalt tile wall drawn only in CSS. Background #1f3f8f with 72px tiles: grout lines (two 2px linear-gradients in rgba(255,255,255,.14)), a turquoise quatrefoil in each tile centre (four small radial-gradients at 50%±8px), and white 5px pips at tile corners, which join into a continuous lattice. A soft vignette radial-gradient to #16306e sits at the edges. Centred on it is the medallion `cn-semse`: max-width 940px, min-height 520px, background #fffefa with a top-left glaze gloss, border-radius 50% (a horizontal ellipse). Its rings are stacked box-shadows that follow the ellipse: 0 0 0 6px #c8402e, 0 0 0 11px #fffdf8, 0 0 0 15px #2fa4a9, 0 0 0 19px #fffdf8, plus a 0 30px 60px rgba(8,18,52,.45) drop. Two salbek pendants sit on the major axis (left and right, outside the ellipse): a 2px cobalt stem ending in a 34px coral lozenge with a white three-dot çintemani. Premium firms get the coral 'Seçkin' seal, which other owners see as visible status worth asking about, and that conversation happens on WhatsApp. Firm registrations: coral is reserved for the register action, so the header 'Firmanızı ekleyin' button and the CTA button are the only large red elements on the page. Counters render only when the real numbers are large enough (≥25 firms, ≥3 categories, ≥3 cities), so a young directory never looks empty. metaphor: A shopkeeper's desk card file (kartvizitlik / Rolodex) on kraft paper. Every firm is a real 85x55 mm business card. Categories are coloured file dividers ('Çekmeceler'), cities are small card boxes, the search form is a ruled index card ('Arama fişi'), and owner sign-up is the blank card at the end of the file ('Boş kart · senin yerin'). The information-design idea is a strict card grammar called 'Kart dili'. Every card answers KİM / NE / NEREDE / NASIL ULAŞIRIM in fixed slots, and the phone number is always the largest text, in the same bottom-left place. Card stock and marks show status: black stock = öne çıkan (premium), red seal = onaylı, green edge notch = şu an açık, dashed blank card = senin yerin. Colour also tells you what an action does: ink black means search or call, green means open or WhatsApp, and red is used ONLY for 'Kartını bırak' (registration). After two cards a visitor knows where the number is, and an owner sees exactly what their own card will look like.
why_unique: The uniqueness comes from the fixed hierarchy of a business card, a format every Turkish esnaf already reads, rather than from decoration. Compared with the closest themes: sun-listing has a marker H1, rounded visual cards, Outfit and yellow; this theme uses proportional paper cards with phone-first slab numerals instead. swipe-cards is a phone-shell swipe deck; this is a desktop desk with a static rack, and only the hero fan spreads on hover. design-catalog has a TOC, Nº numbering, dot leaders and Fraunces; here the dividers are physical staggered tabs and there are no dot leaders. board-v2, classifieds-board and ilan-board use pins, cork, newsprint and dense 3-column portals, none of which appear here. paper-trail, city-journal and elegant use serif mastheads, datelines and Georgia or Playfair; this theme has no masthead and uses a slab serif (Zilla Slab), which no other theme uses. craft-market uses a brick-red primary; here red is a small registration accent and the primary is warm carbon ink. index-rally is an A-Z letter index; here categories are colour-coded file dividers. local-ledger is a civic register; this theme feels like a shopkeeper's desk instead. It also avoids every crowded pattern: no photo hero, no phone shell, no Leaflet map, no 3-column rail, no 50/50 split, no 2x3 tile grid, and no green, blue or purple primary. There are no uppercase eyebrows (divider-tab labels replace them), no 01/02 numbering, no initial-letter avatar squares (with no logo the name simply takes the space), no pill chips and no stats strip (the counts live on the card-file label). The kraft desk (#c9a979) with multi-stock cards (cream, white, kraft, sage, black) is not used anywhere else.
fonts: Heading: Zilla Slab 500/600/700, used for H1, H2, firm names and phone numbers. Body and UI: Archivo 400/500/600/700. Both fonts ship the latin-ext subset, so Turkish ğ ş ı İ ç ö ü render correctly. The config entry sets font_heading to 'Zilla Slab',serif (googleFontsUrl trims the quotes and gives Zilla+Slab) and font_body to Archivo,sans-serif. ThemeHelper::googleFontsUrl only loads a family without weights, so partials/kartvizitlik/styles.blade.php also adds its own preconnect and link: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Zilla+Slab:wght@500;600;700&family=Archivo:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap. Phone numbers use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums, and the number column also gets a fixed min-width so alignment holds even where the font has no tnum. No Georgia, Inter or monospace anywhere.

metaphor: A desk-top business-card file box (kartvizitlik). Every firm is a letterpress business card in standard Turkish kartvizit proportions (85×55, aspect-ratio 85/55). Categories are coloured index dividers with staggered tabs. Districts are the card's "Adres" line, used as a second filter. The hero is a desk pad (sümen) with stitched plum leather corners, where a blank card holds the search and a small fanned pile of real cards lies under it. The whole browse loop happens on the home page with no page loads and zero required JS. You pick a divider (category), narrow by semt (district), toggle "Şu an açık" or "Onaylı", then turn a card over by its folded corner to read the back (description, address, WhatsApp, profile). Native radios plus :has() do the filtering, CSS counters show a live count, and <details name> handles the flip. UI vocabulary: kart = firma, bölme = kategori, kutu = the listing, semt = ilçe, masa = hero, notlar = blog. No numbers-in-circles, no A–Z, no pills.
why_unique: No existing theme has in-page filtering across facets. Today a category or city is always a link to another page. This theme filters the home page itself on four facets (bölme × semt × açık × onaylı) with radio/checkbox inputs plus :has(), shows a live CSS-counter tally, and flips cards in 3D with native <details name> (no theme uses rotateY, backface-visibility or <details> on the home page today). It is also the first home page to use districts as a browse facet, built from the eager-loaded company->district relations. Contrast with the closest themes: swipe-cards is a dark phone-shell Tinder deck of cover-photo cards you swipe away. Here the cards are light, text-only letterpress kartvizits in a responsive full-width page, they stay in a filterable box and turn over in place, and there are no photos and no swiping. index-rally uses numbered queue rows and A–Z letter chips. This theme has no letters and no numbering; categories are physical divider tabs in a 6-colour stationery cycle. design-catalog and paper-trail are printed matter (TOC, dot leaders, mastheads, Georgia/Fraunces), while this is a stationery object (box, dividers, foil, deboss) set in a slab serif. board-v2 and classifieds-board are walls of pinned notes and columns, with no pins, cork or columns here. sun-listing and local-ledger list photo or row cards under a centred or left hero. Here the hero is a desk pad with leather corners, the search is itself a business card, and stats sit in a copper label-holder plate instead of a stats strip. pocket-stories, story-reels and social-feed use category rings; this theme has no rings or avatars, and the initial-letter square is replaced by a two-letter foil or debossed monogram seal. Palette: aubergine/plum primary (#4b2142) with copper foil on a felt-grey desk is used by no theme. It avoids the crowded green, blue/navy, red and violet primaries and the cream+rust+Georgia cluster. Type: Zilla Slab (slab serif, unused) with variable-width Archivo (unused), so 12 divider labels fit three across at 360px. It is not a phone shell, not a photo hero, not a map, not a 3-column portal, not a split hero and not a copy-left/tile-grid hero.
fonts: Heading: Zilla Slab 500/600/700 plus italic 500/600 (letterpress slab, latin-ext, so ç ğ ı İ ö ş ü are covered). Body/UI: Archivo variable (wdth 75–100, wght 400–800, latin-ext). Its width axis lets divider-tab labels use font-stretch:80% at 360px and normal width elsewhere; phone numbers use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Load them in partials/card-file/styles.blade.php with preconnect plus <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo:wdth,wght@75..100,400..800&family=Zilla+Slab:ital,wght@0,500;0,600;0,700;1,500;1,600&display=swap">. The TEMPLATES entry sets font_body 'Archivo,sans-serif' and font_heading "'Zilla Slab',serif" (googleFontsUrl's extra request is harmless). Uppercase title lines rely on <html lang="tr"> (already set in layouts.app), so 'i' becomes 'İ' correctly. Do not use font-variant-caps small-caps: synthesized small caps ignore the Turkish locale. 2 · Kart kutusu (#kutu), the signature section. H2 'Kutudaki kartlar' in Zilla Slab, with a small stacked 6-colour edge mark at its left instead of an uppercase eyebrow. Intro: 'Bir bölme seçin, semte göre daraltın, kartı köşesinden çevirip arkasını okuyun.' The box (.kv-box: background #e3ddd3, inner back wall #d9d3c9, top inset shadow so it reads as an open box) holds, in order:
(a) Divider tabs: <fieldset> with a visually hidden legend 'Bölme'. A default radio #kv-c-all ('Bütün bölmeler', rendered as a full-width copper label-holder plate at the box front), then one radio per category, id kv-c-{index 0..11} (index-based ids, never slugs). Each sr-only input is followed by a label face shaped as a trapezoid tab (clip-path polygon(10px 0,calc(100% - 10px) 0,100% 100%,0 100%)) filled with the cycle colour (--tab = colour index % 6). Tabs sit in grid repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr)) with a row overlap of -6px, so the rows look like stacked dividers; each row ends in a 3px divider-sheet line. The checked tab rises translateY(-6px) and gains shadow.
(b) Address line: fieldset 'Semt' (a default radio #kv-d-all 'Hepsi' plus up to 10 radios kv-d-{i}) built from the distinct districts of the rack, ordered by in-box count. Duplicate names get the city in parentheses ('Merkez (Kayseri)'). It falls back to rack cities, labelled 'Şehir', when there are fewer than 2 districts, and is hidden when there are fewer than 2 values. Options are typographic words separated by '·', each with a superscript in-box count; the checked one gets a plum fill and a 3px copper underline. One horizontally scrolling line on phone.
(c) Status switches (checkboxes #kv-open 'Şu an açık', #kv-ver 'Onaylı'), rendered only if some rack card isOpenNow()===true or is_verified.
(d) A view toggle (radios #kv-view-kutu / #kv-view-masa: 'Kutuda' / 'Masaya diz'), shown below 640px only.
(e) The rack: <ol class=kv-rack> of up to 24 business cards. Rack = premium→trusted→open→latest→map, concat()->unique('id')->take(24), so aggregates come from the first occurrence. Each <li> carries data-c (category index or 'x'), data-d (district/city index), data-open and data-ver when applicable.
(f) Per-category 'more' cards (only the one matching the checked tab is shown). Text: '{Kategori} bölmesinin tamamı · {companies_count} kart →' linking categories.show, with a second line '{Kategori} işletmesi misiniz? Kartınızı bu bölmeye ekleyin' → owner.register. The 'all' version links companies.index ('Bütün kartlar →').
(g) A blank dashed 'cut-out' card 'Bu kutuda kartın yok mu? Kartını ekle' → owner.register, always last.
(h) Tally line 'Kutuda şu an N kart', where N is a CSS counter.
The filter rules (~3 per category, 1 per district) are generated in an inline <style> inside the home view, e.g. `.kv-box:has(#kv-c-3:checked) .kv-rack>li:not([data-c="3"]){display:none}` and the matching more-card/tint rules. The static rules (#kv-open, #kv-ver, view toggle) live in the styles partial.
